title: Prakrama 3, Sarga 9. The Rule on Eating the Remnants of Offerings to Shiva
html:
At Bhubaneshvara the Lord longs for Shiva's prasada and, when it is brought, partakes of it with reverence; Murari explains to Damodara Pandita why Bhrigu's curse does not touch the remnants of offerings to Shiva when he is worshipped as the best of Vaishnavas

Verse 1

स्नात्वा स बिन्दुसरसि दृष्ट्वा श्रीभुवनेश्वरम्।
सुखमासीनो भगवान्प्रेमानन्दपरिप्लुतः॥१॥

snātvā sa bindusarasi dṛṣṭvā śrībhuvaneśvaram|
sukhamāsīno bhagavānpremānandapariplutaḥ||1||

snatva — having bathed; sah — He; bindu-sarasi — in the Bindu lake; drishtva — having seen; shri-bhuvaneshvaram — Sri Bhuvaneshvara; sukham — happily; asinah — sat; bhagavan — Bhagavan; prema-ananda-pariplutah — steeped in the bliss of love.

1Having bathed in the Bindu lake1 and beheld Sri Bhuvaneshvara2, Bhagavan, steeped in the bliss of love, sat at rest in happiness.

Verse 2

ततो भुक्त्वा वरान्नं स भक्तैः सङ्कल्पितं प्रभुः।
सुष्वाप तत्र संहृष्टो ध्यायन्कृष्णपदाम्बुजम्॥२॥

tato bhuktvā varānnaṁ sa bhaktaiḥ saṅkalpitaṁ prabhuḥ|
suṣvāpa tatra saṁhṛṣṭo dhyāyankṛṣṇapadāmbujam||2||

tatah — then; bhuktva — having eaten; vara-annam — excellent food; sah — He; bhaktaih — by the devotees; sankalpitam — dedicated (offered); prabhuh — the Lord; sushvapa — slept; tatra — there; samhrishtah — joyful; dhyayan — meditating; krishna-pada-ambujam — on the lotus feet of Krishna.

2Then the Lord ate the excellent food offered by the devotees and joyfully went to sleep there, meditating on the lotus feet of Krishna.

Verse 3

चिन्तयामास भगवान्देवदेवस्य शूलिनः।
महाप्रसादो लभ्येत तदा भुज्यामहे वयम्॥३॥

cintayāmāsa bhagavāndevadevasya śūlinaḥ|
mahāprasādo labhyeta tadā bhujyāmahe vayam||3||

chintayam asa — thought; bhagavan — Bhagavan; deva-devasya — of the god of gods; shulinah — the Bearer of the trident; maha-prasadah — the mahaprasada; labhyeta — could be had; tada — then; bhujyamahe — would eat; vayam — we.

3Bhagavan thought, "If only we could have the mahaprasada of the god of gods, the Bearer of the trident, we would partake of it."

Verse 4

इति चिन्तयतस्तस्य महादेवप्रसादकम्।
पाणिभ्यां ब्राह्मणः कश्चिदादाय सम्मुखे स्थितः॥४॥

iti cintayatastasya mahādevaprasādakam|
pāṇibhyāṁ brāhmaṇaḥ kaścidādāya sammukhe sthitaḥ||4||

iti — thus; chintayatah — as He was thinking; tasya — He; mahadeva-prasadakam — Mahadeva's prasada; panibhyam — in both hands; brahmanah — a brahmana; kashchit — certain; adaya — holding; sammukhe — before Him; sthitah — stood.

4As He was thinking thus, a certain brahmana came and stood before Him, holding Mahadeva's prasada in both hands,

Verse 5

उवाच च महादेवप्रसादं गृह्यतामिति।
तच्छ्रुत्वा सहसोत्थाय गृहीत्वा शिरसा नमः॥५॥

uvāca ca mahādevaprasādaṁ gṛhyatāmiti|
tacchrutvā sahasotthāya gṛhītvā śirasā namaḥ||5||

uvacha — said; cha — and; mahadeva-prasadam — Mahadeva's prasada; grihyatam — let it be accepted; iti — thus; tat — that; shrutva — hearing; sahasa — at once; utthaya — rising; grihitva — receiving; shirasa — on His head; namah — with obeisance.

5and said, "Please accept the prasada of Mahadeva." Hearing this, the Lord at once rose, received it on His head with an obeisance,

Verse 6

महाप्रसादं संगृह्य पपौ भृत्यैः सुधामिव।
शिवप्रियो हि श्रीकृष्ण इति संदर्शयन्हरिः॥६॥

mahāprasādaṁ saṁgṛhya papau bhṛtyaiḥ sudhāmiva|
śivapriyo hi śrīkṛṣṇa iti saṁdarśayanhariḥ||6||

maha-prasadam — the mahaprasada; samgrihya — receiving; papau — partook (lit. drank); bhrityaih — with His servants; sudham — nectar; iva — like; shiva-priyah — one to whom Shiva is dear; hi — indeed; shri-krishnah — Sri Krishna; iti — that; sandarshayan — showing; harih — Hari.

6and, taking the mahaprasada, partook of it with His servants as though it were nectar: thus Hari showed that Shiva is dear to Sri Krishna.

Verse 7

सुखाय पुनरेवासौ प्रातरुत्थाय सत्वरः।
स्नात्वा वै बिन्दुसरसि शिवं नत्वा ययौ हरिः॥७॥

sukhāya punarevāsau prātarutthāya satvaraḥ|
snātvā vai bindusarasi śivaṁ natvā yayau hariḥ||7||

sukhaya — in joy; punah — again; eva — indeed; asau — He; pratah — in the morning; utthaya — rising; satvarah — in haste; snatva — bathing; vai — indeed; bindu-sarasi — in the Bindu lake; shivam — to Shiva; natva — bowing; yayau — went on; harih — Hari.

7In the morning Hari again rose in haste, full of joy, bathed in the Bindu lake, bowed to Shiva and went on His way.

Verse 8

एतन्निशम्य देवस्य शिवनिर्माल्यभक्षणम्।
प्रत्युवाच महातेजाः श्रीदामोदरपण्डितः॥८॥

etanniśamya devasya śivanirmālyabhakṣaṇam|
pratyuvāca mahātejāḥ śrīdāmodarapaṇḍitaḥ||8||

etat — this; nishamya — hearing; devasya — of the Lord; shiva-nirmalya-bhakshanam — the eating of the remnants of offerings to Shiva; pratyuvacha — replied; maha-tejah — of great power; shri-damodara-panditah — Sri Damodara Pandita.

8Hearing how the Lord had eaten the nirmalya3 of Shiva, Sri Damodara Pandita, a man of great power, objected:

Verse 9

नाश्नाति शिवदेवस्य निर्माल्यं भृगुशापतः।
कथं ज्ञात्वा स भगवान्बुभुजे तन्नरोत्तमः॥९॥

nāśnāti śivadevasya nirmālyaṁ bhṛguśāpataḥ|
kathaṁ jñātvā sa bhagavānbubhuje tannarottamaḥ||9||

na ashnati — (one) does not eat; shiva-devasya — of the god Shiva; nirmalyam — the remnants of offerings; bhrigu-shapatah — because of Bhrigu's curse; katham — how; jnatva — knowing; sah — He; bhagavan — Bhagavan; bubhuje — ate; tat — that; nara-uttamah — the best of men.

9"The nirmalya of the god Shiva is not eaten, because of Bhrigu's curse4. How then could Bhagavan, the best of men, knowing this, have eaten it?"

Verse 10

तच्छ्रुत्वा प्राह विप्रेन्द्रं मुरारिः श्रूयतामिति।
कथां श्रीशिवदेवस्य निर्माल्यामृतभक्षणे॥१०॥

tacchrutvā prāha viprendraṁ murāriḥ śrūyatāmiti|
kathāṁ śrīśivadevasya nirmālyāmṛtabhakṣaṇe||10||

tat — that; shrutva — hearing; praha — said; vipra-indram — to the best of brahmanas; murarih — Murari; shruyatam — let it be heard; iti — thus; katham — the account; shri-shiva-devasya — of Sri Shiva; nirmalya-amrita-bhakshane — about the eating of the nectar of the remnants of offerings.

10Hearing this, Murari said to the best of brahmanas, "Listen to the story of the nectar of Sri Shiva's nirmalya.

Verse 11

वस्तुतस्तु महादेवः श्रीकृष्णस्य शुभागमे।
आतिथ्यं विदधे हर्षात्तेन किं च परं शृणु॥११॥

vastutastu mahādevaḥ śrīkṛṣṇasya śubhāgame|
ātithyaṁ vidadhe harṣāttena kiṁ ca paraṁ śṛṇu||11||

vastutah — in truth; tu — indeed; mahadevah — Mahadeva; shri-krishnasya — of Sri Krishna; shubha-agame — on the auspicious arrival; atithyam — hospitality; vidadhe — offered; harshat — with joy; tena — for that reason; kim cha — moreover; param — further; shrinu — hear.

11In truth, when Sri Krishna made His auspicious arrival, Mahadeva joyfully offered Him hospitality — that is why He partook of it. But hear more.

Verse 12

वैष्णवश्रेष्ठबुद्ध्या ये पूजयन्ति महेश्वरम्।
तैर्दत्तं गृह्णते सोऽपि तदन्नं पावनं महत्॥१२॥

vaiṣṇavaśreṣṭhabuddhyā ye pūjayanti maheśvaram|
tairdattaṁ gṛhṇate so'pi tadannaṁ pāvanaṁ mahat||12||

vaishnava-shreshtha-buddhya — regarding him as the best of Vaishnavas; ye — who; pujayanti — worship; maheshvaram — Maheshvara; taih — by them; dattam — offered; grihnate — accepts; sah — He; api — too; tat — that; annam — food; pavanam — purifying; mahat — greatly.

12When people worship Maheshvara, regarding him as the best of Vaishnavas5, He too accepts what they offer; such food is supremely purifying.

Verse 13

श्रीकृष्णकृष्णभक्तानां भेदबुद्ध्या पतन्त्यधः।
दुर्वैरान्शिक्षयंस्तांश्च भक्तरूपः स्वयं हरिः॥१३॥

śrīkṛṣṇakṛṣṇabhaktānāṁ bhedabuddhyā patantyadhaḥ|
durvairānśikṣayaṁstāṁśca bhaktarūpaḥ svayaṁ hariḥ||13||

shri-krishna-krishna-bhaktanam — of Sri Krishna and Krishna's devotees; bheda-buddhya — by the notion of difference; patanti — fall; adhah — down; durvairan — the malignantly hostile; shikshayan — teaching; tan — them; cha — and; bhakta-rupah — in the form of a devotee; svayam — Himself; harih — Hari.

13Those who see a difference between Sri Krishna and Krishna's devotees fall down. And to teach such malignant opponents, Hari Himself, in the form of a devotee —

Verse 14

आचरत्यपि देवेशो हितकृत्सर्वदेहिनाम्।
निर्माल्यमादरेणैव गृहीत्वा जगदीश्वरः॥१४॥

ācaratyapi deveśo hitakṛtsarvadehinām|
nirmālyamādareṇaiva gṛhītvā jagadīśvaraḥ||14||

acharati — practises it Himself; api — indeed; deva-ishah — the Lord of the gods; hita-krit — the benefactor; sarva-dehinam — of all embodied beings; nirmalyam — the remnants of offerings; adarena — with reverence; eva — indeed; grihitva — accepting; jagat-ishvarah — the Lord of the world.

14the Lord of the gods, the Lord of the world, the benefactor of all embodied beings — Himself does as He teaches: He accepts the nirmalya with reverence.

Verse 15

जनैः संस्थापिते लिङ्गे भेदबुद्ध्या च पूजिते।
तत्रैव शापो विप्रस्य नहि स्यादैक्यतः क्वचित्॥१५॥

janaiḥ saṁsthāpite liṅge bhedabuddhyā ca pūjite|
tatraiva śāpo viprasya nahi syādaikyataḥ kvacit||15||

janaih — by people; samsthapite — installed; linge — in the case of a linga; bheda-buddhya — with the notion of difference; cha — and; pujite — worshipped; tatra — there; eva — only; shapah — the curse; viprasya — of the brahmana (Bhrigu); na hi — by no means; syat — applies; aikyatah — where there is oneness; kvachit — ever.

15The brahmana's curse applies only where a linga has been installed by people and is worshipped with a notion of difference; where there is oneness, it never applies.

Verse 16

हरिशङ्करयोरैक्यं स्वयम्भूलिङ्गसन्निधौ।
अभेदबुद्ध्या पूजायां नहि शापो भवेत्क्वचित्॥१६॥

hariśaṅkarayoraikyaṁ svayambhūliṅgasannidhau|
abhedabuddhyā pūjāyāṁ nahi śāpo bhavetkvacit||16||

hari-shankarayoh — of Hari and Shankara; aikyam — oneness; svayambhu-linga-sannidhau — in the presence of a self-manifest linga; abheda-buddhya — with the notion of non-difference; pujayam — in worship; na hi — by no means; shapah — the curse; bhavet — is; kvachit — ever.

16In the presence of a self-manifest linga6 Hari and Shankara are one7; when worship is offered with a sense of non-difference, the curse never applies.

Verse 17

तेन तत्राधिका प्रीतिर्हरिशङ्करयोर्भवेत्।
अभेदेऽत्र स्वयम्भौ च पूजा सर्वातिशायिनी॥१७॥

tena tatrādhikā prītirhariśaṅkarayorbhavet|
abhede'tra svayambhau ca pūjā sarvātiśāyinī||17||

tena — therefore; tatra — there; adhika — greater; pritih — the pleasure; hari-shankarayoh — of Hari and Shankara; bhavet — is; abhede — in non-difference; atra — here; svayambhau — to the self-manifest (linga); cha — and; puja — worship; sarva-atishayini — surpassing all.

17Therefore Hari and Shankara are still more pleased there; and the worship of the self-manifest linga here, in non-difference, surpasses all.

Verse 18

महाप्रसादं तत्रैव भुक्त्वा मोक्षमवाप्नुयात्।
महारोगात्प्रमुच्येत स्थिरसम्पत्तिमाप्नुयात्॥१८॥

mahāprasādaṁ tatraiva bhuktvā mokṣamavāpnuyāt|
mahārogātpramucyeta sthirasampattimāpnuyāt||18||

maha-prasadam — the mahaprasada; tatra — there; eva — indeed; bhuktva — eating; moksham — liberation; avapnuyat — will attain; maha-rogat — from grave disease; pramuchyeta — will be freed; sthira-sampattim — lasting prosperity; apnuyat — will gain.

18Whoever eats the mahaprasada there will attain liberation, be freed from grave disease and gain lasting prosperity.

Verse 19

ये मोहात्तन्न खादन्ति ते भवन्त्यपराधिनः।
हरौ शिवे च निःश्रीका रोगिणश्च भवन्ति ते॥१९॥

ye mohāttanna khādanti te bhavantyaparādhinaḥ|
harau śive ca niḥśrīkā rogiṇaśca bhavanti te||19||

ye — who; mohat — out of delusion; tat — it; na khadanti — do not eat; te — they; bhavanti — become; aparadhinah — offenders; harau — against Hari; shive — against Shiva; cha — and; nihshrikah — bereft of fortune; roginah — diseased; cha — and; bhavanti — become; te — they.

19But those who out of delusion do not eat it become offenders against Hari and Shiva, lose their fortune and fall ill.

Verse 20

वैष्णवैः पूजितो यत्र श्रीशिवः परमादरात्।
अनादिलिङ्गमासाद्य श्रीकृष्णप्रीतिहेतवे॥२०॥

vaiṣṇavaiḥ pūjito yatra śrīśivaḥ paramādarāt|
anādiliṅgamāsādya śrīkṛṣṇaprītihetave||20||

vaishnavaih — by Vaishnavas; pujitah — worshipped; yatra — where; shri-shivah — Sri Shiva; parama-adarat — with the greatest reverence; anadi-lingam — the beginningless linga; asadya — approaching; shri-krishna-priti-hetave — for the pleasure of Sri Krishna.

20Wherever Vaishnavas come to the beginningless linga and worship Sri Shiva with the greatest reverence for the pleasure of Sri Krishna,

Verse 21

तत्रैव संशयो नास्ति निर्माल्यग्रहणे क्वचित्।
भक्तिरेव सदा विप्र शुभदा सर्वदेहिनाम्॥२१॥

tatraiva saṁśayo nāsti nirmālyagrahaṇe kvacit|
bhaktireva sadā vipra śubhadā sarvadehinām||21||

tatra — there; eva — indeed; samshayah — doubt; na asti — there is no; nirmalya-grahane — in accepting the remnants of offerings; kvachit — any; bhaktih — devotion; eva — alone; sada — always; vipra — O brahmana; shubha-da — bestows good; sarva-dehinam — on all embodied beings.

21there is no doubt at all about accepting the nirmalya. Devotion alone, O brahmana, always brings good to all embodied beings."

Thus ends the ninth sarga, "The Rule on Eating the Remnants of Offerings to Sri Shiva" (Shri-shiva-nirmalya-bhojana-vyavastha), of the third prakrama of the poem "Sri Krishna-chaitanya-charitamrita."

✦

Notes

  1. The Bindu lake is the Bindu-sarovara, the sacred pond of Bhubaneshvara (see Sarga 3.08, v. 7).
  2. Bhuvaneshvara ("Lord of the Worlds") is Shiva as worshipped at Ekamraka (Krittivasa, Sarga 3.08); the town itself takes its name from him.
  3. Nirmalya: the remnants (flowers, food, etc.) of offerings made to a deity.
  4. At Daksha's sacrifice the sage Bhrigu cursed the followers of Shiva (Bhagavata Purana 4.2); the prohibition against eating the remnants of offerings to Shiva was traced to this. Damodara Pandita is the listener to whom Murari tells this account (cf. Sarga 3.01, v. 1).
  5. Cf. Bhagavata Purana 12.13.16: "As Shambhu is the best of Vaishnavas…"
  6. That is, a linga that has manifested of itself, not one installed by people (v. 15).
  7. Murari sets the "oneness" (aikya) and "non-difference" (abheda) of Hari and Shankara (vv. 15–17) against the "notion of difference" (bheda-buddhi), in which Shiva is worshipped as a god separate from Krishna and independent of Him — a rival of Hari. To worship Shiva "without difference" is to see in him the best of Vaishnavas (v. 12), inseparable from Krishna as the Lord's devotee is inseparable from Him (v. 13), and to honour him for the pleasure of Krishna (v. 20). This does not make Shiva equal to Vishnu: according to the Brahma-samhita (5.45), Shiva is non-different from Govinda as curd is from the milk it came from — and yet he is not Govinda Himself; and the Padma Purana calls one who regards the demigods, Shiva among them, as equal to Narayana an apostate (pashandi).
